<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par108 />''since I have seen thy face''; and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=8}}. In the 1st pers. plur. the cohortative includes a summons to others to help in doing something, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=נְנַתְּקָה|translate=come! let us break asunder!}} &c., and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|108|c}}
(''b'') To express a wish, or a request for permission, that one should be allowed to do something, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶעְבְּרָה|translate=may I be allowed to pass through}} (''let me pass through'')! {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=נַעְבְּרָה־נָּא|translate=may we be allowed to pass through!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=15}} ''let me go, I pray thee!'' &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=9}}; so after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=14}}; after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=25|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַל־אֵב֫וֹשָׁה|translate=let me not be ashamed}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=2}}, 18, 71:1); 69:15. After {{GHGheb|text=אַל־נָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=1|verse=14}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|108|d}}
'''2.''' The cohortative in dependence on other moods, as well as in conditional sentences: (''a'') In dependence (with {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=15}} after {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן}}) on an imperative or jussive to express an intention or intended consequence, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=4}} ''bring it to me'', {{GHGheb|text=וְאֹכֵ֑לָה|translate=that I may eat}}, prop. ''then will I eat''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=56|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=25|hidebook=1}} f., 42:34, 49:1, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=20}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=19}} ''and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw nigh and come'', {{GHGheb|text=וְנֵדָֽעָה|translate=that we may know}} (''it'')! {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=27|verse=5}}. Also after negative sentences, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=30}}, 32, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=39}}, and after interrogative sentences, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=5}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|108|e}}
(''b'') In conditional sentences (with or without {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}) to express a contingent intention, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=אִם־אֲדַבְּרָה|translate=should I determine to speak, my grief is not assuaged}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְאַחְדְּלָה|translate=and should I forbear, what am I eased?}} without {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=26|hidebook=1}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=וָאיחלה}} is probably intended); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=16}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲח׳}} should be read), 139:8 f. After the 3rd person, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=17}} ''though it be dark'', &c. So perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=38}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶרְדְּפָה|translate=if I determined to pursue, then}} ..., but cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=38}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|108|f}}
(''c'') Likewise in the apodosis of conditional sentences, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=7}} f. ''if my step hath turned out of the way'' ..., {{GHGheb|text=אֶזְרְעָה|translate=then let me sow}}; cf. 16:4 f. ''I also could speak as ye do, if ...!'' So even when the condition must be supplied from the context, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=6}} ''else would I declare and speak of them''; 51:18 ''else would I'' (''gladly'') ''give it'', i.e. if thou didst require it (cf. the precisely similar {{GHGheb|text=וְאֶשָּׂא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=13}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=10}}. In the 1st plur. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=10}}. To the same category belong the cohortatives after the formula expressing a wish {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתֵּן}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתְּנֵ֫נִי}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=1}} ''oh, that I had'' ..., {{GHGheb|text=וְאֶֽעֶזְבָה|translate=then}} (i.e. if I had) ''should I'' (or ''would I'') ''leave my people'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=29}}; without {{GHGterm|Wāw}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=4}} (cf. also verse 7).

{{GHGmargin-letter|108|g}}
Rem. 1. The question, whether a resolution formed under compulsion (a ''necessity'') is also expressed by the cohortative (so, according to the prevailing opinion, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵלֵ֫כָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, 21, 6:10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=3}}, 18 (?); 57:5, where, however, with Hupfeld, {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁכְבָה}} should be read; 77:7, 88:16, and in the 1st plur. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=10}}), is to be answered in the sense that in these examples the cohortative ''form'' is used after its meaning has become entirely lost, merely for the sake of its fuller sound, instead of the ordinary imperfect. This view is strongly<section end=par108 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
